title: Cost Reduction Initiative — Experiment Cadence & Runbook (batching, caching, quantization)
creator: Sophie Chen
description: This ticket captures the initiative-level runbook and experiment cadence for unlocking recurring token cost savings across Redwood's inference surface. Scope includes controlled field experiments on batching parameters, prefix/KV caching heuristics, and model quantization profiles across hosted and dedicated runtimes. The goal is to standardize hypothesis design, rollout gates, measurement, and rollback criteria so PM/Eng/Research can run parallel low-risk experiments and reliably translate wins into rollout policies and console recommendations.
acceptance_criteria: A reproducible experiment template (hypothesis, variants, telemetry, duration, success metrics) adopted by Eng and Research
Three pilot experiments executed end-to-end (batch size tuning, aggressive KV prefetch, 4-bit quant profile) with clear signal/noise analysis
Automated dashboard tile(s) in Console that surface experiment-level cost delta and quality regression within 48 hours of experiment completion
Runbook for rollouts that maps experiment outcomes to rollout actions: automatic policy, staged rollout, or revert
metrics: Primary: delta token cost per 1M output tokens (USD)
Quality guardrails: semantic similarity drop vs baseline (embedding cosine) and prompt-level error rate (%)
Operational: experiment churn (number of variant flips) and rollback frequency

experiments: Batch Tuning — Hypothesis: modestly increasing max_batch_size for short sequences (<=64 tokens) will reduce per-token compute cost by 8-12% with <2% tail-latency impact. Variants: baseline, +20% batch, +50% batch. Metrics: cost delta, p95 latency, request queueing rate. Duration: 2 weeks.

KV Prefetch Heuristic — Hypothesis: enabling prefix prefetch with an LRU hotset (top 5% request prefixes) reduces repeated autoregressive KV recomputation and yields 6-10% savings on chat-heavy workloads. Variants: baseline, hotset size 3%, 5%, 10%. Metrics: token cost, cache hit ratio, freshness decay. Safety: rollback if user-facing hallucination rate increases >0.5%.

Quant Profile Sweep — Hypothesis: moving certain mid-capacity models to an adaptive 4-bit quant profile reduces GPU memory pressure and unit cost by 18-25% with minimal degradation for structured output tasks. Variants: baseline FP16, static 8-bit, adaptive 4-bit for low-sensitivity routes. Metrics: model quality evals on curated prompt set, memory utilization, throughput delta. Security note: run within private/dedicated pools first.
